title: Development of Natural Resources & Afforestation
source_note: Standard NUC-aligned Nigerian university 400L Botany/Plant Science curriculum on natural resource management: classification of renewable/non-renewable resources, forest resources and Nigerian vegetation zones, causes and effects of deforestation, afforestation and reforestation techniques, agroforestry systems, forest management and silviculture, conservation strategies, watershed and range management, and sustainable development principles relevant to Nigeria/West Africa.

questions.question: Natural resources are broadly classified into renewable and non-renewable types. Which of the following is a renewable natural resource?
options: Crude petroleum
Coal
Forest (timber) resources
Natural gas
questions.correct_answer: Forest (timber) resources
questions.explanation: Forests can regenerate naturally or be replanted, making them renewable if managed sustainably, unlike fossil fuels (petroleum, coal, gas) which form over geological timescales and are non-renewable on human timescales.

questions.question: Which of Nigeria's major vegetation zones is characterised by tall, multi-storeyed evergreen trees, high biodiversity and high annual rainfall (over 2000 mm)?
options: Sahel savanna
Sudan savanna
Tropical rainforest
Desert
questions.correct_answer: Tropical rainforest
questions.explanation: Nigeria's tropical rainforest belt in the south has high rainfall and humidity supporting dense, multi-layered evergreen forest with the highest species diversity among Nigerian vegetation zones.

questions.question: Moving from south to north, the general sequence of Nigeria's vegetation zones is:
options: Sahel savanna, Guinea savanna, rainforest, mangrove
Mangrove/coastal, rainforest, derived savanna, Guinea savanna, Sudan savanna, Sahel savanna
Desert, rainforest, mangrove
Rainforest only throughout the country
questions.correct_answer: Mangrove/coastal, rainforest, derived savanna, Guinea savanna, Sudan savanna, Sahel savanna
questions.explanation: Nigeria's vegetation transitions from coastal mangrove and rainforest in the south, through derived and Guinea savanna in the middle belt, to Sudan and Sahel savanna in the drier far north, reflecting the north-south rainfall gradient.

questions.question: Deforestation is best defined as:
options: The planting of new trees in a previously forested area
The permanent removal or clearing of forest cover, usually for other land use, without adequate regeneration
The natural succession of a forest
The scientific management of forest resources
questions.correct_answer: The permanent removal or clearing of forest cover, usually for other land use, without adequate regeneration
questions.explanation: Deforestation refers to the conversion of forested land to non-forest uses (agriculture, settlement, logging without replanting) resulting in net loss of forest cover.

questions.question: Which of the following is a major direct driver of deforestation in Nigeria?
options: Afforestation programmes
Expansion of subsistence and commercial agriculture into forest land
Establishment of forest reserves
Reduction in human population
questions.correct_answer: Expansion of subsistence and commercial agriculture into forest land
questions.explanation: Agricultural land expansion (shifting cultivation, commercial farming, plantation establishment) is one of the leading drivers of forest loss in Nigeria, along with logging, fuelwood extraction and urbanisation.

questions.question: One major ecological consequence of large-scale deforestation is:
options: Increased soil erosion and loss of soil fertility
Increased groundwater recharge in all cases
Decreased atmospheric carbon dioxide
Improved local microclimate stability
questions.correct_answer: Increased soil erosion and loss of soil fertility
questions.explanation: Removal of tree cover exposes soil to raindrop impact and runoff, accelerating erosion and nutrient loss, and disrupts the water cycle and local climate.

questions.question: Desertification, a serious problem in northern Nigeria, is best described as:
options: The process by which fertile land becomes increasingly arid and degraded, losing vegetation and productivity, often due to deforestation, overgrazing and climate factors
The natural expansion of tropical rainforest
The conversion of desert to fertile farmland
A type of afforestation technique
questions.correct_answer: The process by which fertile land becomes increasingly arid and degraded, losing vegetation and productivity, often due to deforestation, overgrazing and climate factors
questions.explanation: Desertification results from a combination of climatic variability and unsustainable human activities (overgrazing, deforestation, poor irrigation) that degrade land in dryland regions such as Nigeria's Sahel belt.

questions.question: Afforestation is defined as:
options: Replanting trees on land that was recently forest
Establishing forest/trees on land that was not previously forested, or has not been forested for a long time
The complete removal of all trees from an area
The process of timber harvesting
questions.correct_answer: Establishing forest/trees on land that was not previously forested, or has not been forested for a long time
questions.explanation: Afforestation is planting trees on land that historically lacked forest cover (e.g. savanna, degraded land), distinguished from reforestation which restores recently cleared forest land.

questions.question: Reforestation differs from afforestation in that reforestation specifically refers to:
options: Planting trees on land that never had forest
Re-establishing forest on land that was recently deforested or degraded forest land
Cutting down existing forest
Building irrigation canals in forests
questions.correct_answer: Re-establishing forest on land that was recently deforested or degraded forest land
questions.explanation: Reforestation restores tree cover on land that was forested in the recent past but was cleared or degraded, as opposed to afforestation on historically non-forest land.

questions.question: The 'Great Green Wall' initiative in Nigeria and the Sahel region is primarily aimed at:
options: Building a physical wall to stop migration
Combating desertification and land degradation through large-scale tree planting and sustainable land management across the Sahel
Expanding urban housing estates
Increasing crude oil exploration
questions.correct_answer: Combating desertification and land degradation through large-scale tree planting and sustainable land management across the Sahel
questions.explanation: The Great Green Wall is a pan-African initiative involving a mosaic of tree planting, land restoration and sustainable agriculture to halt desert encroachment across the Sahel, including northern Nigeria.

questions.question: Shelterbelts (windbreaks) established in afforestation programmes serve primarily to:
options: Reduce wind speed, protect crops/soil from wind erosion, and moderate microclimate
Increase soil salinity
Attract more pests to farmland
Serve only ornamental purposes
questions.correct_answer: Reduce wind speed, protect crops/soil from wind erosion, and moderate microclimate
questions.explanation: Shelterbelts are rows of trees planted to reduce wind velocity, thereby limiting wind erosion, reducing evapotranspiration, and creating a more favourable microclimate for crops, common in Sahel afforestation schemes.

questions.question: Which tree species is commonly recommended for afforestation/shelterbelt establishment in the semi-arid Sahel zone of Nigeria because of its drought tolerance?
options: Rhizophora mangle (mangrove)
Eucalyptus camaldulensis
Nypa palm
Water hyacinth
questions.correct_answer: Eucalyptus camaldulensis
questions.explanation: Eucalyptus camaldulensis (river red gum) is widely used in dryland afforestation and shelterbelt projects in the Sahel because of its fast growth and drought tolerance; mangroves and Nypa are coastal/wetland species, not suited to arid zones.

questions.question: Agroforestry is a land-use system that:
options: Excludes trees entirely from agricultural land
Deliberately combines trees/shrubs with crops and/or livestock on the same land management unit
Focuses only on monoculture timber plantations
Is practised only in temperate countries
questions.correct_answer: Deliberately combines trees/shrubs with crops and/or livestock on the same land management unit
questions.explanation: Agroforestry integrates woody perennials with crops and/or animals to achieve complementary benefits -- soil improvement, shade, fodder, fuelwood -- and is widely promoted in Nigerian land-use and afforestation planning.

questions.question: In the taungya agroforestry system practised in parts of Nigeria, farmers are permitted to:
options: Grow food crops between young forest tree seedlings during the early establishment years in exchange for tending the trees
Clear forest reserves permanently for farmland
Graze cattle exclusively without any tree planting
Harvest mature timber without replanting
questions.correct_answer: Grow food crops between young forest tree seedlings during the early establishment years in exchange for tending the trees
questions.explanation: The taungya system allows farmers to intercrop food crops with newly planted forest tree seedlings, benefiting both the farmer (food) and the forestry agency (tended, weeded plantation) until canopy closure.

questions.question: Alley cropping, an agroforestry technique, involves:
options: Planting food crops in alleys between rows of nitrogen-fixing trees/shrubs that are periodically pruned
Clear-felling all trees before planting crops
Growing only ornamental trees along roads
A method used exclusively for fish farming
questions.correct_answer: Planting food crops in alleys between rows of nitrogen-fixing trees/shrubs that are periodically pruned
questions.explanation: Alley cropping arranges crops between hedgerows of trees (often leguminous, e.g. Leucaena, Gliricidia) that are pruned to provide mulch/green manure and reduce shading, improving soil fertility and structure.

questions.question: Silviculture is best defined as:
options: The scientific management of forest establishment, composition, growth and quality to meet specific objectives
The study of soil chemistry only
The classification of animal species in forests
A method of fish preservation
questions.correct_answer: The scientific management of forest establishment, composition, growth and quality to meet specific objectives
questions.explanation: Silviculture is the branch of forestry concerned with controlling forest establishment, growth, composition and quality through practices such as thinning, pruning and selective felling.

questions.question: The 'clear-felling' (clear-cutting) silvicultural system involves:
options: Removing all trees in a stand at once, followed by regeneration (natural or artificial)
Selectively removing only diseased trees
Never harvesting any trees
Only thinning young trees
questions.correct_answer: Removing all trees in a stand at once, followed by regeneration (natural or artificial)
questions.explanation: Clear-felling harvests an entire stand in one operation, after which the site is regenerated, contrasted with selection systems that remove only mature or selected trees while retaining others.

questions.question: The 'selection system' of silviculture, in contrast to clear-felling, involves:
options: Periodically removing individual mature trees or small groups, maintaining a continuous, multi-aged forest cover
Removing the entire forest in a single operation
Planting a single species only
Never allowing any harvesting
questions.correct_answer: Periodically removing individual mature trees or small groups, maintaining a continuous, multi-aged forest cover
questions.explanation: The selection system harvests mature trees individually or in small groups at intervals, maintaining an uneven-aged, continuous forest canopy and reducing soil exposure compared to clear-felling.

questions.question: Thinning in silviculture refers to:
options: Complete removal of a forest stand
The periodic removal of some trees from a stand to reduce competition and improve growth of remaining trees
Planting more trees into an already dense stand
A method of seed storage
questions.correct_answer: The periodic removal of some trees from a stand to reduce competition and improve growth of remaining trees
questions.explanation: Thinning selectively removes weaker, diseased, or overcrowded trees to reduce competition for light, water and nutrients, promoting better growth and quality in the remaining stand.

questions.question: A forest reserve, as designated under Nigerian forestry law, is primarily intended to:
options: Permanently protect and manage forest land for sustainable production, conservation and ecological services
Allow unrestricted logging by anyone
Convert forest land immediately to urban development
Serve no legal protective function
questions.correct_answer: Permanently protect and manage forest land for sustainable production, conservation and ecological services
questions.explanation: Forest reserves are legally gazetted areas set aside for sustainable forest management, protecting them from uncontrolled clearing while allowing regulated exploitation and conservation.

questions.question: Which of the following best distinguishes a national park from a forest reserve in Nigeria?
options: National parks are managed primarily for strict conservation of biodiversity and ecotourism, with little or no extractive use, unlike forest reserves which may allow regulated timber extraction
National parks allow unrestricted logging while forest reserves do not
They are functionally identical with no difference
National parks exist only outside Nigeria
questions.correct_answer: National parks are managed primarily for strict conservation of biodiversity and ecotourism, with little or no extractive use, unlike forest reserves which may allow regulated timber extraction
questions.explanation: National parks (e.g. Yankari, Cross River, Old Oyo) emphasise wildlife and habitat conservation with tourism, generally prohibiting logging and hunting, whereas gazetted forest reserves can permit sustainable timber and non-timber extraction.

questions.question: In-situ conservation of plant genetic resources refers to:
options: Conserving species within their natural habitat, e.g. in protected forest reserves or national parks
Storing seeds in a seed bank away from the natural habitat
Growing plants in botanical gardens only
Freezing plant tissue in liquid nitrogen
questions.correct_answer: Conserving species within their natural habitat, e.g. in protected forest reserves or national parks
questions.explanation: In-situ conservation protects species and their genetic diversity within the ecosystems where they naturally occur, complementing ex-situ methods (seed banks, botanical gardens, tissue culture) that conserve them outside their natural habitat.

questions.question: Ex-situ conservation of plant genetic resources includes which of the following approaches?
options: Seed banks, botanical gardens, and field gene banks
Only protecting species inside national parks
Leaving species entirely undisturbed in the wild
Only regulating hunting laws
questions.correct_answer: Seed banks, botanical gardens, and field gene banks
questions.explanation: Ex-situ conservation conserves genetic material outside natural habitats, using seed banks, botanical/arboreta collections, field gene banks and tissue culture repositories.

questions.question: Sustainable development, as it applies to natural resource use, is generally defined as development that:
options: Maximises short-term resource extraction regardless of future consequences
Meets the needs of the present generation without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs
Focuses exclusively on economic growth ignoring the environment
Prohibits any use of natural resources
questions.correct_answer: Meets the needs of the present generation without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs
questions.explanation: This is the widely accepted Brundtland Commission (1987) definition of sustainable development, balancing present needs with intergenerational equity in resource use.

questions.question: Which of the following farming/land-use practices contributes to sustainable land and forest resource management?
options: Continuous monoculture with no fallow or rotation
Bush burning of forest land before every planting season
Crop rotation, agroforestry and controlled, rotational fallow systems
Uncontrolled logging without replanting
questions.correct_answer: Crop rotation, agroforestry and controlled, rotational fallow systems
questions.explanation: Crop rotation, agroforestry and managed fallow maintain soil fertility and vegetation cover, supporting long-term productivity, unlike continuous monoculture, indiscriminate burning or unregulated logging.

questions.question: Non-timber forest products (NTFPs) important to rural livelihoods in Nigeria include which of the following?
options: Sawn timber planks only
Bushmeat, medicinal plants, fruits, gums and resins, and fibres
Crude oil
Manufactured furniture
questions.correct_answer: Bushmeat, medicinal plants, fruits, gums and resins, and fibres
questions.explanation: NTFPs encompass all forest products other than timber -- bushmeat, medicinal plants, fruits, nuts, gums, resins, fibres and fodder -- which are economically and nutritionally important to many rural communities.

questions.question: Watershed management is primarily concerned with:
options: The integrated management of land, vegetation and water resources within a drainage basin to control runoff, erosion and water quality
Constructing dams without regard to vegetation
Managing only fish populations in rivers
Urban housing planning
questions.correct_answer: The integrated management of land, vegetation and water resources within a drainage basin to control runoff, erosion and water quality
questions.explanation: Watershed management integrates soil, vegetation and water conservation practices across a catchment area to regulate streamflow, reduce erosion/sedimentation, and maintain water quality and supply.

questions.question: Vegetation cover in a watershed helps regulate water resources mainly by:
options: Increasing surface runoff and flash flooding
Intercepting rainfall, promoting infiltration, and reducing surface runoff and erosion
Preventing all rainfall from reaching the soil
Having no effect on the hydrological cycle
questions.correct_answer: Intercepting rainfall, promoting infiltration, and reducing surface runoff and erosion
questions.explanation: Vegetation canopy and root systems intercept rainfall, slow overland flow, and enhance soil infiltration, reducing peak runoff, flooding risk and erosion within a watershed.

questions.question: Overgrazing, a major cause of rangeland degradation in northern Nigeria, occurs when:
options: Livestock numbers and grazing pressure exceed the regenerative capacity of the pasture, leading to vegetation loss and soil exposure
Livestock are rotated systematically among paddocks
Grazing is completely excluded from an area
Pasture productivity always increases regardless of stocking rate
questions.correct_answer: Livestock numbers and grazing pressure exceed the regenerative capacity of the pasture, leading to vegetation loss and soil exposure
questions.explanation: Overgrazing depletes palatable forage species faster than they can regenerate, leading to bare soil, erosion, and encroachment of unpalatable or invasive plants, contributing to desertification.

questions.question: Rotational grazing is a rangeland management practice that helps prevent overgrazing by:
options: Allowing continuous, unrestricted grazing on a single paddock indefinitely
Moving livestock periodically among different paddocks/pastures to allow vegetation recovery time
Eliminating grazing entirely
Increasing stocking density permanently
questions.correct_answer: Moving livestock periodically among different paddocks/pastures to allow vegetation recovery time
questions.explanation: Rotational grazing rests grazed paddocks to allow forage regrowth, maintaining rangeland productivity and preventing the vegetation degradation associated with continuous overgrazing.

questions.question: The Forestry Research Institute of Nigeria (FRIN) is primarily responsible for:
options: Conducting research on forestry, forest products and afforestation techniques to support sustainable forest management in Nigeria
Managing Nigeria's petroleum reserves
Regulating banking activities
Building national highways
questions.correct_answer: Conducting research on forestry, forest products and afforestation techniques to support sustainable forest management in Nigeria
questions.explanation: FRIN, headquartered in Ibadan, is Nigeria's principal forestry research institute, generating knowledge and planting materials for afforestation, silviculture and forest products development.

questions.question: One key ecological benefit of urban afforestation (tree planting in towns/cities) is:
options: Increased air pollution
Reduction of the urban heat island effect and improvement of air quality
Increased soil erosion in cities
Elimination of all rainfall
questions.correct_answer: Reduction of the urban heat island effect and improvement of air quality
questions.explanation: Urban trees provide shade and evapotranspirative cooling that reduce the urban heat island effect, while also filtering airborne pollutants and particulates.

questions.question: Which factor most limits the success of afforestation projects in Nigeria's Sahel/Sudan savanna zones?
options: Excessive rainfall causing flooding of seedlings
Low and erratic rainfall combined with high evapotranspiration, causing high seedling mortality
Absence of any soil
Too much shade from existing tall forest
questions.correct_answer: Low and erratic rainfall combined with high evapotranspiration, causing high seedling mortality
questions.explanation: The arid/semi-arid climate of the Sahel and Sudan savanna zones subjects newly planted seedlings to moisture stress, making species selection (drought-tolerant species) and establishment timing critical for afforestation success.

questions.question: Community/social forestry programmes aim primarily to:
options: Exclude local communities entirely from forest resource decisions
Involve local communities directly in tree planting, forest protection and management to meet local needs and improve livelihoods
Transfer all forest land to government control with no local input
Focus solely on export-oriented timber production
questions.correct_answer: Involve local communities directly in tree planting, forest protection and management to meet local needs and improve livelihoods
questions.explanation: Community/social forestry engages local people as active participants and beneficiaries in planting, protecting and managing forest resources, improving both conservation outcomes and rural livelihoods.
